content.comment_body: Hello, I am currently working with a [product_name] version [version_no] of type [article_no]. Communication is set up using the S7 protocol. I understand that, in general, it is possible to read the CPU state (RUN / STOP / HALTED) on controllers like [version_no]. However, I haven't found documentation confirming whether the [product_name] allows reading the CPU state, nor details on how this can be achieved. Since the CPU state is important when working with [product_name] variables, I am interested in how one can determine the CPU state during runtime through the S7 protocol. Thanks in advance, Greetings,

With the [product_name], this should generally work, but I am not aware of any possibility for a [product_name] user to query the status directly. Also, these devices are quite different from [version_no] controllers in terms of functionality. In such cases, [company_name] often provides limited access to diagnostics. I typically address this using a watchdog approach: a signal is generated on the remote side that changes state every second and is sent to the [product_name] (for example, V0.0). The [product_name] then returns this signal unchanged (such as V0.1). The remote side evaluates the response; if the signal's status remains unchanged for more than 1.5 seconds, either communication is disrupted or the [product_name] is in STOP mode.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to monitor the CPU status (RUN/STOP/HALTED) on a [product_name] via the S7 protocol, similar to methods applied on [version_no] controllers. However, there is a lack of clear documentation or direct support for querying this status on [product_name], leading users to implement workarounds such as custom signaling and watchdog logic. This highlights the less straightforward diagnostic capabilities of [product_name] compared to more advanced [version_no] controllers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like to directly access the CPU state (RUN/STOP/HALTED) of the [product_name] at runtime using the S7 protocol, similar to what is possible with [version_no] controllers.
